title: Where the Water Comes From
text:
Turn on a tap in Singapore and the water arrives without drama, as though it had always been there. It has not. This island has no rivers worth the name and no natural lakes, and for much of its history it depended almost entirely on what fell from the sky or arrived through a pipeline from across the Strait.
The response was neither modest nor quick. Streams were dammed to create reservoirs. Drains were widened into a network that catches rain across two thirds of the island. Used water is collected, cleaned to an extraordinary standard, and returned to the taps. Seawater is pushed through membranes fine enough to strain out salt.
None of it is free, and none of it is permanent. The engineers who built these systems solved the problem for their generation. Keeping the tap running belongs to the next one.
